fields.Name: Endorheic basin
fields.Description: A drainage area with no outlet to the sea; its water leaves only by evaporation or seepage.
fields.Notes: The Caspian Sea, the Great Basin of the western United States and Lake Eyre are examples.
fields.Caption 1: The endorheic basin that feeds Üüreg Lake, Mongolia
fields.Caption 2: The endorheic Tarim Basin, China, from space
fields.Caption 3: The endorheic Altiplano basin at La Paz and El Alto, Bolivia

fields.Name: Cirque
fields.Description: An armchair-shaped hollow at the head of a valley, carved into a mountainside by a glacier.
fields.Notes: Often holds a small lake called a tarn once the ice has gone.
fields.Caption 1: Two cirques with snow patches near Abisko, Sweden
fields.Caption 2: Maritsa cirque in the Rila Mountains, Bulgaria
fields.Caption 3: Upper Thornton Lake cirque, North Cascades, Washington

fields.Name: Caldera
fields.Description: A large basin-shaped depression left when a volcano collapses after emptying its magma chamber.
fields.Notes: Crater Lake in Oregon fills one about 8 km wide, formed about 7,700 years ago.
fields.Caption 1: Lake Toba, Sumatra, in a caldera 100 km long
fields.Caption 2: Valles Caldera, New Mexico
fields.Caption 3: The summit caldera of Fernandina, Galápagos

fields.Name: Glacier
fields.Description: A large, persistent body of ice that forms on land from compacted snow and slowly flows downhill under its own weight.
fields.Notes: About a tenth of Earth's land is covered by ice of this kind, most of it in Antarctica and Greenland.
fields.Caption 1: The Baltoro Glacier, Pakistan
fields.Caption 2: The Taschachferner in the Ötztal Alps, Austria
fields.Caption 3: The Quelccaya Ice Cap, Peru

fields.Name: Rift lake
fields.Description: A body of water that fills a trough formed where the crust is pulling apart.
fields.Notes: Lake Baikal, the deepest lake on Earth, and Lake Tanganyika are the great examples.
fields.Caption 1: Lake Baikal at the Svyatoy Nos peninsula, where the fault scarp shows active rifting
fields.Caption 2: Rift lakes of the Albertine Rift, East Africa (rendering)
fields.Caption 3: Children on the shore of Lake Malawi at Nkhata Bay

fields.Name: Fjord
fields.Description: A long, narrow, steep-sided sea inlet cut by a glacier and later flooded by the ocean.
fields.Notes: Norway, Chile, New Zealand, Greenland, and British Columbia have the most famous ones.
fields.Caption 1: Geirangerfjord, Norway
fields.Caption 2: Milford Sound, New Zealand
fields.Caption 3: A glacier flowing through a fjord in eastern Greenland

fields.Name: Arête
fields.Description: A thin, knife-edged ridge left between two glacial valleys or hollows that have eroded toward each other.
fields.Notes: Striding Edge in England's Lake District is a well-known example.
fields.Caption 1: Crib Goch, Snowdonia, Wales
fields.Caption 2: Clouds Rest, Yosemite National Park
fields.Caption 3: The Garden Wall, Glacier National Park

fields.Name: Pyramidal peak
fields.Description: A sharp, steep-sided summit shaped by glaciers eroding several hollows back to back around it.
fields.Notes: The Matterhorn is the classic example.
fields.Caption 1: The Matterhorn, Switzerland, and Italy
fields.Caption 2: Alpamayo, Peru
fields.Caption 3: Artesonraju, Peru

fields.Name: U-shaped valley
fields.Description: A steep-walled, flat-floored trough with a rounded cross-section, widened and deepened by a glacier.
fields.Notes: A river valley, by contrast, is V-shaped in cross-section.
fields.Caption 1: A glaciated valley in the Altai Mountains, Russia
fields.Caption 2: Myklebustdalen, Nordfjord, Norway
fields.Caption 3: Malyovitsa valley, Rila Mountains, Bulgaria

fields.Name: Moraine
fields.Description: A ridge or heap of rock and debris carried and dropped by a glacier.
fields.Notes: Long Island, New York, is largely built of the moraines of the last ice sheet.
fields.Caption 1: Lateral and terminal moraines around a lake near Manang, Nepal
fields.Caption 2: Moraine of the Nanga Parbat north-face glacier, Pakistan
fields.Caption 3: A glacier and its terminal moraine at Tinayrebukta, Svalbard

fields.Name: Drumlin
fields.Description: A smooth, elongated hill of glacial deposits shaped like an inverted spoon, with its steeper end facing the ice's approach.
fields.Notes: They occur in swarms, sometimes by the thousand, as in Ireland's Clew Bay.
fields.Caption 1: Forested drumlins south of Puerto Williams, Chile
fields.Caption 2: Clew Bay, Ireland, a field of drowned drumlins
fields.Caption 3: A farm on a drumlin

fields.Name: Esker
fields.Description: A long, winding ridge of sand and gravel laid down by a stream running through or beneath a glacier.
fields.Notes: Some in Finland and Canada run for hundreds of kilometres.
fields.Caption 1: An esker at Fulufjället, Sweden
fields.Caption 2: A partly drowned esker at Billudden, Sweden
fields.Caption 3: Esker at Sims Corner, Washington

fields.Name: Kettle lake
fields.Description: A round, water-filled hollow left when a stranded block of glacier ice melted.
fields.Notes: Cape Cod and Minnesota have thousands of them.
fields.Caption 1: A kettle in the Isunngua highland, Greenland
fields.Caption 2: Kettle lakes on the Yamal Peninsula, Siberia
fields.Caption 3: Kettle lakes beside the Denali Highway, Alaska

fields.Name: Glacial erratic
fields.Description: A boulder carried far from its source by ice and left behind on rock of a different kind.
fields.Notes: Big Rock in Alberta is a quartzite boulder that travelled hundreds of kilometres.
fields.Caption 1: Erratics from Norway on Schokland, Netherlands
fields.Caption 2: A glacial erratic in Snowdonia, Wales
fields.Caption 3: Erratics on a terminal moraine in Washington State

fields.Name: Hanging valley
fields.Description: A side channel that ends high above the floor of the main trough it joins, often with a waterfall.
fields.Notes: It arises because the main valley was cut deeper by a larger glacier.
fields.Caption 1: Muldalsfossen drops from the Muldalen hanging valley to Tafjorden, Norway
fields.Caption 2: Gleann Gaorsaic, a hanging valley in Scotland
fields.Caption 3: Hanging glacial valley of Kukaj, Albanian Alps

fields.Name: Oxbow lake
fields.Description: A curved body of water formed when a loop is cut off from the river's main channel.
fields.Notes: The name comes from the U-shaped collar of an ox's yoke.
fields.Caption 1: Oxbow lakes beside the South Fork of the Koyukuk River, Alaska
fields.Caption 2: Oxbow lakes of the Taieri River, New Zealand
fields.Caption 3: An oxbow lake in Hokkaido, Japan

fields.Name: Meander
fields.Description: One of a series of sinuous loops in a river's course, caused by erosion on the outer bank and deposition on the inner.
fields.Notes: The Mississippi has shifted its course by many kilometres through its meanders.
fields.Caption 1: Meanders of the Río Cauto, Cuba
fields.Caption 2: Meanders of the Uvac River, Serbia
fields.Caption 3: An incised meander of the Shimanto River, Japan

fields.Name: Delta
fields.Description: A low, fan-shaped landform built where a stream drops its sediment on entering a sea or lake.
fields.Notes: Named after the Greek letter Δ, whose shape Herodotus saw in the triangular mouth of the Nile.
fields.Caption 1: The Nile Delta in false colour, from space
fields.Caption 2: The Lena Delta, Russia
fields.Caption 3: The Amazon Delta, from space

fields.Name: Alluvial fan
fields.Description: A cone-shaped deposit of gravel and sand spread where a mountain stream emerges onto a plain.
fields.Notes: Death Valley has many.
fields.Caption 1: An alluvial fan in the French Pyrenees
fields.Caption 2: A large alluvial fan in Death Valley
fields.Caption 3: An alluvial fan in the Taklamakan Desert, Xinjiang

fields.Name: Floodplain
fields.Description: The flat land beside a river that is covered by water when the river overflows.
fields.Notes: Its rich silt has made such land the site of ancient agriculture along the Nile, Tigris, and Euphrates.
fields.Caption 1: The Paraná River floodplain
fields.Caption 2: The River Eden's floodplain under water, England
fields.Caption 3: The Laramie River at the site of Fort John, Wyoming

fields.Name: Estuary
fields.Description: A partly enclosed coastal water body where fresh river water meets and mixes with the salt water of the sea.
fields.Notes: Chesapeake Bay is the largest in the United States.
fields.Caption 1: The Río de la Plata estuary
fields.Caption 2: The New York–New Jersey Harbor estuary
fields.Caption 3: An estuary mouth at Darwin, Australia

fields.Name: Canyon
fields.Description: A deep, steep-sided valley cut through rock, usually by a river.
fields.Notes: The Grand Canyon is about 446 km long and up to 1.8 km deep.
fields.Caption 1: Sumidero Canyon, Mexico
fields.Caption 2: Snake River Canyon, Idaho
fields.Caption 3: The Grand Canyon, at the Little Colorado River confluence

fields.Name: Mesa
fields.Description: A flat-topped, steep-sided landform wider than it is tall, left when erosion strips away the surrounding rock.
fields.Notes: The word is Spanish for table.
fields.Caption 1: Mesas in Monument Valley, on the Colorado Plateau
fields.Caption 2: Mount Garfield, a mesa in Colorado
fields.Caption 3: Har Qatum, a mesa beside Makhtesh Ramon, Israel

fields.Name: Butte
fields.Description: An isolated, steep-sided hill with a small flat top, taller than it is wide.
fields.Notes: Monument Valley in Arizona and Utah is dotted with them.
fields.Caption 1: The Mittens and Merrick Butte, Monument Valley
fields.Caption 2: Devils Tower, Wyoming
fields.Caption 3: Courthouse Butte, Sedona, Arizona

fields.Name: Plateau
fields.Description: An extensive area of high, relatively flat land that is bounded by steep slopes on at least one side.
fields.Notes: The Tibetan Plateau, at over 4,500 m average height, is the highest in the world.
fields.Caption 1: The Tibetan Plateau from space
fields.Caption 2: The Pajarito Plateau from the Clinton P. Anderson overlook, Los Alamos
fields.Caption 3: The Chajnantor Plateau in the Atacama, Chile

fields.Name: Escarpment
fields.Description: A long, steep slope or cliff that separates two level areas of different height.
fields.Notes: The Niagara Escarpment runs from New York State through Ontario to Wisconsin.
fields.Caption 1: Cliffs of the Niagara Escarpment on Georgian Bay, Bruce Peninsula
fields.Caption 2: The Niagara Escarpment in winter
fields.Caption 3: The Great Escarpment of southern Africa

fields.Name: Inselberg
fields.Description: An isolated rock hill or small mountain rising sharply from a surrounding plain.
fields.Notes: Uluru in central Australia is the most famous example.
fields.Caption 1: Uluru, Australia
fields.Caption 2: Pietra di Bismantova, Italy
fields.Caption 3: Cono de Arita, Argentina

fields.Name: Yardang
fields.Description: A streamlined, wind-sculpted ridge of rock, aligned with the prevailing wind.
fields.Notes: The Lut Desert in Iran has some of the largest in the world.
fields.Caption 1: Kaluts, or yardangs, in the Lut Desert, Iran
fields.Caption 2: Yardangs at Dunhuang, China
fields.Caption 3: Yardangs in Qinghai, China

fields.Name: Dune
fields.Description: A mound or ridge of loose sand heaped by the wind.
fields.Notes: Those of the Namib Desert reach over 300 m high.
fields.Caption 1: Dunes of Maspalomas, Gran Canaria
fields.Caption 2: Star dunes in Great Sand Dunes National Park, Colorado
fields.Caption 3: Dunes of the Rub' al Khali, from space

fields.Name: Playa
fields.Description: A flat, dry lakebed in a desert basin that fills with shallow water after rain.
fields.Notes: Bonneville Salt Flats in Utah is a well-known example.
fields.Caption 1: Racetrack Playa, Death Valley
fields.Caption 2: Black Rock Desert playa, Nevada
fields.Caption 3: The Alvord Desert playa, Oregon

fields.Name: Karst
fields.Description: A landscape formed by the dissolving of soluble rock such as limestone, marked by sinkholes, caves, and underground streams.
fields.Notes: The name comes from the Kras plateau of Slovenia and Italy.
fields.Caption 1: Cone karst on the Li River, Guilin, China
fields.Caption 2: Karst terrain of the Dinaric Alps, Croatia
fields.Caption 3: Karst formation in the Serra de Tramuntana, Mallorca

fields.Name: Sinkhole
fields.Description: A hollow in the ground caused when the surface collapses into a void formed by dissolved rock below.
fields.Notes: The Great Blue Hole off Belize is a marine one, over 300 m across.
fields.Caption 1: The Red Lake sinkhole, Imotski, Croatia
fields.Caption 2: Sinkholes near the Dead Sea
fields.Caption 3: A collapse sinkhole in Chinchón, Spain

fields.Name: Stalactite
fields.Description: A mineral formation hanging from the roof of a cave, formed by dripping water that deposits calcite.
fields.Notes: A way to remember it: it holds tight to the ceiling.
fields.Caption 1: Cave formations, with stalactites hanging from the roof
fields.Caption 2: Shark-tooth stalactites
fields.Caption 3: Stalactites in the Bear Cave, Kletno, Poland

fields.Name: Stalagmite
fields.Description: A mound that rises from the floor of a cave, built up from mineral left by water dripping from above.
fields.Notes: It may join the one overhead to form a column.
fields.Caption 1: The Witch's Finger, Carlsbad Caverns, New Mexico
fields.Caption 2: Stalagmites in the Coves d'Artà, Mallorca
fields.Caption 3: Stalagmites in Għar Dalam cave, Malta

fields.Name: Geyser
fields.Description: A hot spring that periodically erupts a column of water and steam.
fields.Notes: Old Faithful in Yellowstone erupts about every 90 minutes.
fields.Caption 1: Old Faithful erupting, Yellowstone
fields.Caption 2: Steamboat Geyser, Yellowstone
fields.Caption 3: Strokkur erupting, Iceland

fields.Name: Shield volcano
fields.Description: A broad, gently sloping mountain built up by runny lava flows.
fields.Notes: Mauna Loa in Hawaii is the largest active volcano on Earth by volume.
fields.Caption 1: Mauna Loa's broad shield on the island of Hawaiʻi, from space
fields.Caption 2: Skjaldbreiður, Iceland
fields.Caption 3: The lava lake of Erta Ale, Ethiopia

fields.Name: Stratovolcano
fields.Description: A steep, conical volcano built of alternating layers of lava, ash, and rock fragments.
fields.Notes: Mount Fuji, Vesuvius, and Mount St Helens are all of this type.
fields.Caption 1: Mount Fuji, Japan
fields.Caption 2: Mount Rainier, Washington
fields.Caption 3: Mount Etna, Sicily

fields.Name: Cinder cone
fields.Description: A small, steep volcano built from fragments of lava thrown out around a single vent.
fields.Notes: Parícutin in Mexico appeared in a farmer's cornfield in 1943 and grew to over 300 m in its first year.
fields.Caption 1: Sunset Crater, Arizona
fields.Caption 2: Parícutin, Mexico
fields.Caption 3: Parícutin, Michoacán, Mexico

fields.Name: Lava dome
fields.Description: A rounded mass of thick, sticky molten rock that piles up around a volcanic vent instead of flowing away.
fields.Notes: One grew inside the crater of Mount St Helens between 2004 and 2008.
fields.Caption 1: Lava domes in the crater of Mount St Helens
fields.Caption 2: The rhyolitic lava dome of Chaitén volcano, Chile
fields.Caption 3: One of the Inyo Craters, a rhyolite dome, California

fields.Name: Volcanic plug
fields.Description: A mass of hardened magma that fills the neck of a volcano and, when the cone around it erodes, stands out as a tower.
fields.Notes: Shiprock in New Mexico is a famous example.
fields.Caption 1: The chapel of Saint-Michel d'Aiguilhe on a volcanic plug, Le Puy-en-Velay
fields.Caption 2: A volcanic plug near Rhumsiki, Cameroon
fields.Caption 3: Gros Piton and Petit Piton, Saint Lucia

fields.Name: Batholith
fields.Description: A huge mass of intrusive igneous rock, more than 100 square kilometres in extent, that has cooled deep in the crust.
fields.Notes: Yosemite's granite cliffs are part of the Sierra Nevada one.
fields.Caption 1: The Sierra Nevada Batholith
fields.Caption 2: North Dome and Basket Dome, Yosemite
fields.Caption 3: Half Dome, Yosemite

fields.Name: Dike
fields.Description: A sheet of igneous rock that cuts across the layers of the rock it intrudes.
fields.Notes: When it is harder than its surroundings, erosion leaves it standing as a wall.
fields.Caption 1: A dike cutting horizontal rock layers, Makhtesh Ramon, Israel
fields.Caption 2: A dike beside Shiprock, New Mexico
fields.Caption 3: A composite dike in Orkney, Scotland

fields.Name: Sill
fields.Description: A sheet of igneous rock that has been squeezed between layers of older rock and runs parallel to them.
fields.Notes: The Whin Sill of northern England carries much of Hadrian's Wall.
fields.Caption 1: Salisbury Crags, Edinburgh, a dolerite sill
fields.Caption 2: A dolerite sill at Horton Bluff, Nova Scotia
fields.Caption 3: High Force waterfall, which drops over the Whin Sill, England

fields.Name: Horst
fields.Description: A block of the crust that stands raised between two faults with lower ground on either side.
fields.Notes: The Black Forest and the Vosges are the horsts flanking the Rhine Graben.
fields.Caption 1: Horst and graben in the Basin and Range, western United States
fields.Caption 2: The Black Forest rising above the Rhine plain
fields.Caption 3: Kiger Gorge on Steens Mountain, Oregon, a tilted fault-block range

fields.Name: Graben
fields.Description: A block of the crust that has dropped between two roughly parallel faults.
fields.Notes: The Rhine Graben, between the Vosges and the Black Forest, is one.
fields.Caption 1: Death Valley, a graben, below the Panamint Range
fields.Caption 2: Deep Springs Valley, California
fields.Caption 3: The Rhine Graben seen from the Black Forest

fields.Name: Rift valley
fields.Description: A long, low trough formed where the crust is being pulled apart, with steep walls along its edges.
fields.Notes: The East African Rift is splitting the continent and will one day form a new ocean.
fields.Caption 1: The Great Rift Valley in Kenya
fields.Caption 2: The Manda-Hararo rift, Afar, Ethiopia
fields.Caption 3: Lakes of the African Rift Valley, from space

fields.Name: Atoll
fields.Description: A ring-shaped coral reef, or chain of coral islets, that encloses a central lagoon.
fields.Notes: Darwin proposed that it forms as a volcanic island sinks and the reef around it keeps growing upward.
fields.Caption 1: Tetiʻaroa atoll, French Polynesia
fields.Caption 2: Penrhyn atoll, Cook Islands
fields.Caption 3: Rangiroa atoll, French Polynesia

fields.Name: Barrier island
fields.Description: A long, narrow sandy landmass that lies parallel to a coast and is separated from it by a lagoon or bay.
fields.Notes: Padre Island in Texas is the longest in the world.
fields.Caption 1: Mantoloking, New Jersey, on a barrier island
fields.Caption 2: North Stradbroke Island, Queensland, from space
fields.Caption 3: South Padre Island, Texas

fields.Name: Tombolo
fields.Description: A sand or gravel bar that joins an island to the mainland or to another island.
fields.Notes: Monte Argentario in Italy is joined to the mainland by three of them.
fields.Caption 1: The tombolo joining St Ninian's Isle to Shetland
fields.Caption 2: A tombolo near Karystos, Euboea, Greece
fields.Caption 3: The tombolo linking Ap Lei Pai to Ap Lei Chau, Hong Kong

fields.Name: Spit
fields.Description: A narrow strip of sand or shingle joined to the land at one end and pointing out into open water at the other.
fields.Notes: Spurn Head in England and the Hel Peninsula in Poland are well-known ones.
fields.Caption 1: Farewell Spit, South Island, New Zealand
fields.Caption 2: The Curonian Spit from the air
fields.Caption 3: The Curonian Spit from the air

fields.Name: Sea stack
fields.Description: A steep column of rock standing in the sea, left when the waves erode a headland.
fields.Notes: The Twelve Apostles in Victoria, Australia, are among the most famous.
fields.Caption 1: The Twelve Apostles, Victoria, Australia
fields.Caption 2: Dún Briste sea stack, County Mayo, Ireland
fields.Caption 3: The Old Man of Hoy, Orkney

fields.Name: Natural arch
fields.Description: A rock span formed by erosion, with an opening beneath it.
fields.Notes: Arches National Park in Utah holds more than 2,000 of them.
fields.Caption 1: Delicate Arch, Utah
fields.Caption 2: The Azure Window, Malta, before its collapse in 2017
fields.Caption 3: The Great Arch, Tabuk Province, Saudi Arabia

fields.Name: Tor
fields.Description: A freestanding pile of weathered rock crowning a hill or ridge.
fields.Notes: Dartmoor in England is dotted with them.
fields.Caption 1: Haytor, Dartmoor, England
fields.Caption 2: Combestone Tor, Dartmoor
fields.Caption 3: Cuckoo Rock, Dartmoor

fields.Name: Hoodoo
fields.Description: A tall, thin spire of rock, often capped by a harder stone, left when softer rock has weathered away.
fields.Notes: Bryce Canyon in Utah has the largest collection.
fields.Caption 1: Hoodoos in Bryce Canyon, Utah
fields.Caption 2: Goblin Valley State Park, Utah
fields.Caption 3: Fairy chimneys near Çavuşin, Cappadocia, Turkey

fields.Name: Seamount
fields.Description: A mountain rising from the ocean floor without reaching the surface.
fields.Notes: Most are extinct volcanoes.
fields.Caption 1: Axial Seamount, off Oregon (bathymetry)
fields.Caption 2: Davidson Seamount, off California (bathymetry)
fields.Caption 3: The Eratosthenes Seamount in a bathymetric image

fields.Name: Mid-ocean ridge
fields.Description: An underwater mountain chain where new sea-floor crust is formed as two tectonic plates pull apart.
fields.Notes: Iceland is a part of the Mid-Atlantic one that has risen above the sea.
fields.Caption 1: The age of the ocean floor: the youngest crust, in red, runs along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge
fields.Caption 2: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge in the South Atlantic
fields.Caption 3: The rift of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge on land at Þingvellir, Iceland

fields.Name: Ocean trench
fields.Description: A long, narrow, very deep depression in the deep-sea floor, formed where one tectonic plate dives beneath another.
fields.Notes: The Mariana Trench holds the deepest known point, Challenger Deep, at nearly 11 km.
fields.Caption 1: The Mariana Trench (bathymetry)
fields.Caption 2: The Peru–Chile Trench (bathymetry)
fields.Caption 3: The Puerto Rico Trench

fields.Name: Continental shelf
fields.Description: The gently sloping, shallow seabed that fringes a continent before dropping away steeply.
fields.Notes: Most of the world's fisheries lie above it.
fields.Caption 1: The shelf, slope, and a trench beyond it (schematic)
fields.Caption 2: Fishing on a continental shelf
fields.Caption 3: The Gulf of Mexico shelf and slope in bathymetry
